findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so log assertions no longer observe records
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now emits its log line via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so every record is written into a throwaway `TestLogger` that the test holds no reference to. Any test that injects a `plog.TestLogger` into the middleware and then asserts on `InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message`/`Ctx` will see zero calls, meaning the assertions either fail or (if written as "no error") silently stop verifying anything. `FromContext` (and arguably `New`) should return the same instance (or at least share the `Logs` state) so captured logs remain observable.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname/traceID when used without the contextual logger middleware
findings.body: The explicit log params (`pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `traceID`) were removed and the middleware now relies entirely on contextual attributes injected by the separate, exported `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` plus a registered contextual log provider for the trace ID. There is no compile-time or runtime guarantee of that coupling: `NewLoggerMiddleware` is exported and any stack that omits the contextual logger middleware, or places it after the logger middleware, will produce "Plugin Request Completed" lines with no plugin/datasource/user identification at all — an operationally significant log regression that will not be caught by tests. Also note the trace ID previously came from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` (unsampled spans included); it now depends on whatever the registered contextual log provider does, so the field can disappear for unsampled traces. Either keep the identifying fields in the middleware or document/enforce the ordering dependency and add a test asserting the fields are present in the final log line.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported plugins log.Logger interface is a breaking change
findings.body: `log.Logger` in `pkg/plugins/log` is an exported interface consumed across the plugin packages (and by downstream/enterprise code). Adding the `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` method means every existing implementation outside this repository (or in a repo that vendors it, e.g. grafana-enterprise fakes/wrappers) fails to compile until updated. If the intent is only to let middleware derive a contextual logger, consider a narrower optional interface (type-asserted at the call site) instead of widening the shared interface.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests
findings.body: `contextual_logger_middleware.go` is new behaviour that the logger middleware now depends on (it is the only source of `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` in plugin request logs), yet no test file was added. There is no coverage asserting that the attributes are attached to the context for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, nor that downstream logging actually picks them up, so a regression in either this middleware or its position in the stack would go unnoticed.
